summary: The note describes the fourth section of the Emergency Response Guidebook, identified by orange page borders, which contains the actual response guides. Each of the 62 guides gives safety recommendations and directions for the initial response phase (first thirty minutes) of an incident. Each guide also gives health and fire or explosion hazard information, with the more dangerous hazard listed first.
one_line: Describes the Emergency Response Guidebook's fourth section of 62 response guides, covering initial incident safety steps and listed health and fire or explosion hazards.
key_facts: The fourth section of the Emergency Response Guidebook has orange page borders.
The fourth section of the Emergency Response Guidebook includes the actual response guides.
The Emergency Response Guidebook's fourth section contains 62 guides.
Each guide provides safety recommendations for the initial response phase of an incident.
Each guide gives directions on how to proceed during the initial response phase, which is the first thirty minutes of the incident.
Each guide includes health hazard information.
Each guide includes fire or explosion potential hazard information.
In the Emergency Response Guidebook's guides, the more dangerous hazard is listed first.
An example of fire or explosion hazard wording is: the material gives off irritating vapors, easily ignited by heat, reactive with water.
An example of health hazard wording is: highly toxic, may be fatal if inhaled, swallowed or absorbed through skin.
